meta.title: MIE MATCHA — Japanese Matcha Guide
meta.description: MIE MATCHA: tasting profiles, tea houses, origin context and brewing ritual. A discovery library, not an online shop.

footer.copy: A matcha discovery archive built around tasting, source context, ritual and experience. This is not an online store.
footer.priceNote: Reference prices, when shown, are informational only.

home.heroCopy: Explore matcha through source context, flavor structure, aroma, finish and tea ritual — as a tea library rather than a storefront.
home.introP1: Matcha differs by much more than grade. Source context, tea house, aroma, body, umami, bitterness, sweetness and finish all shape a distinct experience.
home.introP2Before: That is why this archive prioritizes
home.introP2After: over product merchandising — price appears only as secondary reference information when sourced.
home.spectrumAside: A visual sample scale for understanding profiles. Product scores appear only after sourced values are entered in Admin.
home.brandAside: Enter each tea house to read its context, reference region and the tea profiles preserved in this archive.
home.journalAside: Short notes on flavor, preparation, water and storage to make each bowl of matcha easier to understand.

guide.metaDescription: A calm introduction to matcha preparation: Usucha, Koicha and latte context.
guide.lead: An editorial-style guide. Product-specific ratios appear only when sourced values have been entered in Admin.
guide.usucha: A lighter matcha preparation that can emphasize brightness, balance and finish. Use this as an exploration frame; specific ratios require sourced data.
guide.koicha: A denser texture that makes umami and body more apparent. The website does not assign a tea to Koicha unless the source supports it.
guide.latte: Milk changes the perception of bitterness, body and sweetness. Once Admin adds ‘Best for’ data, the library can filter for Latte.
guide.methodCopy: 01 — Sift to reduce clumps. 02 — Choose water volume and temperature from verified profile data. 03 — Whisk with a compact, consistent motion. 04 — Taste in sequence: aroma → first sip → mid-palate → finish.
guide.sourceNote: The 2g / 60–70ml / 70–75°C figures in the brief are UX examples rather than data from matcha.docx, so the project does not automatically seed them into individual teas.

about.metaDescription: Why MIE MATCHA is built as a tasting journal rather than an online shop.
about.lead: MIE MATCHA is designed to help readers understand tea through flavor language, context and ritual — without cart, discount or stock pressure.
about.p1: The website separates ‘tea profile’ from ecommerce thinking. An entry may include a reference price, but price always remains secondary information.
about.p2: Source meaning is preserved. Fields absent from the document — such as brewing ratios, numeric tasting scores or some product-level origins — remain null until Admin can add verified information.
about.p3: The visual language uses paper #EDEAE5, soft matcha #D0E0B3, green #75A35B and tea brown #3B2C19 for a contemporary tea-journal atmosphere.
